rationale: Comprehensive evaluation of biallelic NOTCH3 cohorts in the provided literature demonstrates a consistent genotype-phenotype divergence. Patients carrying biallelic loss-of-function or cysteine-sparing variants uniformly present in infancy or early childhood (typically 9 to 14 months) with global developmental delay, epilepsy, spasticity, visual/oculomotor abnormalities, and early-onset strokes, accompanied by MRI findings of periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia without anterior temporal pole involvement. In contrast, patients carrying biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants exhibit an adult-onset CADASIL-spectrum phenotype (onset in the 3rd to 5th decades) characterized by subcortical lacunar strokes, progressive cognitive decline/dementia, and deep white matter hyperintensities without pronounced volume loss.

evidence.text: Systematic evaluation of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants confirmed distinct genotype-phenotype divergence: 26 patients with biallelic loss-of-function variants developed a childhood neurodevelopmental disorder with spasticity and childhood-onset strokes, whereas 24 patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants presented with an adult CADASIL-spectrum phenotype including adult-onset stroke and dementia.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Our systematic analyses verified distinct genotype-phenotype correlations for the two types of biallelic variants in NOTCH3. Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Three pediatric patients from two families harboring biallelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants presented between 9 and 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, recurrent strokes, and small vessel disease leukoencephalopathy sparing the anterior temporal poles.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both. The disease course was characterized by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes, migraine attacks, and seizures... Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

evidence.text: Two siblings harboring homozygous null nonsense variants (p.Arg735Ter) presented with severe congenital-onset neurodevelopmental manifestations including global developmental delay, epilepsy, pyramidal signs, eye misalignment, and visual impairment.

source.title: Autosomal recessive NOTCH3-related leukodystrophy in two siblings and review of the literature
source.quote: These patients presented with a severe congenital phenotype, including eye misalignment, visual impairment, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and subsequent development of pyramidal signs. Biallelic nonsense variants were discovered in both the cases (NM_000435.3:c.2203 C > T (p. [Arg735Ter]).

evidence.text: A proband with a homozygous NOTCH3 null frameshift variant (c.2984delC) exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and leukoencephalopathy without anterior temporal pole lesions, confirming recessive inheritance and presentation distinct from classic CADASIL.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: WES of the proband identified a novel homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC)... proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

new_directions.question_text: Do compound heterozygous individuals carrying one cysteine-altering allele and one null/LoF allele consistently present with an adult-onset CADASIL phenotype or an intermediate hybrid neurodevelopmental arteriopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Single cases (e.g., p.Cys1146Ser in trans with p.Cys1024Valfs248) manifest adult-onset disease in their mid-thirties, suggesting dominant cysteine-altering gain-of-function effects may override loss-of-function recessive mechanisms, but cohort-wide characterization is needed.

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance of subclinical microvascular and cerebral white matter lesions in heterozygous parents carrying monoallelic NOTCH3 null variants?
new_directions.rationale: Population biobank data indicate monoallelic LoF variants elevate normalized white matter hyperintensity volume without significantly increasing stroke risk, warranting systematic imaging across consanguineous pedigrees.
